articles.title: Sante Raises $15M to Run Wine and Liquor Stores on One AI-Powered Operating System
articles.snippet: Darren Fike took a part-time job at a TriBeCa wine shop to find out why some of the best stores in New York ran on the worst software. What he learned inside an industry of roughly 34,000 independent stores became the basis for AI agents that reprice slow-moving bottles and read distributor invoices on their own. Santé now powers nearly 1,000 stores that process $2B a year, and it just raised $15M to reach thousands more.

articles.text:
Rhino USA Secures $15 Million Asset-Backed Facility From Texas Capital
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 20, 2026
Rhino USA Secures $15 Million Asset-Backed Facility From Texas Capital
Rhino USA has closed a $15 million asset-backed loan facility with Texas Capital to support inventory investment, working capital optimization, and continued expansion across national retail, e-commerce, and international markets.
The Austin, Texas-based company designs truck, towing, and off-road adventure gear and has been expanding across multiple distribution channels, including its own website, Amazon, TikTok Shop, Walmart.com, and retail locations in the U.S., Canada, the U.K., and Europe.
Rhino USA said revenue has doubled over the past two years and quadrupled over the past three years as the company has expanded its product line and customer base. The business now serves millions of customers and employs more than 90 people.
The company was co-founded by brothers Cameron and Dylan Repic, with their father Ted Repic later joining as CEO. Rhino USA began in Murrieta, California, before relocating its headquarters to Austin. Its products are positioned around truck, towing, recovery, and off-road use and are backed by a lifetime guarantee.
The new financing was arranged through Texas Capital’s Asset Based Lending team. Rhino USA plans to use the facility to invest ahead of anticipated demand by increasing inventory levels, strengthening its U.S. distribution network, and supporting hiring in Central Texas and Georgia.
The financing also supports Rhino USA’s broader retail expansion strategy as the company seeks to increase its presence with major national retailers. Management sees inventory availability and supply chain flexibility as important components of maintaining growth as distribution expands across physical retail and digital channels.
Rhino USA is also developing RhinoWorld, a 182-acre brand campus and product proving ground located outside Austin. Plans for the property include an innovation laboratory, content studio, more than eight miles of obstacle terrain, and potential future access for first responder training and community programs. The site is located in a federally designated Opportunity Zone, and Rhino USA said it has already added three full-time positions there in 2026.
The company intends to use RhinoWorld as a location for developing, testing, and demonstrating products under real-world conditions while further expanding its operations in Texas.
KEY QUOTES:
“This financing is a vote of confidence in what we’ve built and where we’re headed. We’ve been on a winning trajectory, and this capital gives us the fuel to sustain that momentum and push even harder. Texas Capital understood our business, our vision and what it takes to win at this level. This collaboration reflects the strength of the platform we’ve spent ten years building, and we’re just getting started.”
Ted Repic, CEO Of Rhino USA
“Inventory depth and supply chain agility are how an American brand competes at national scale. This facility lets us invest ahead of demand in inventory, in our U.S. distribution network, and in the people we’re hiring in Central Texas and Georgia. The Texas Capital team understood that from day one, and having a Texas-based financial services firm with national reach matters as we keep building here.”
Jeremy Bell, COO Of Rhino USA

articles.title: Everphone Secures €15 Million Corporate Loan From Commerzbank And KfW
articles.snippet:
Everphone secured a €15 million corporate loan from Commerzbank and KfW to finance additional workplace devices for its Device-as-a-Service business.
The post Everphone Secures €15 Million Corporate Loan From Commerzbank And KfW appeared first on Pulse 2.0 .
articles.text:
Everphone Secures €15 Million Corporate Loan From Commerzbank And KfW
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 11, 2026
Everphone Secures €15 Million Corporate Loan From Commerzbank And KfW
Everphone secured a €15 million corporate loan from Commerzbank and KfW to finance additional workplace devices for its Device-as-a-Service business.
The company plans to use the proceeds to purchase new laptops, smartphones, tablets, and other workplace devices that are provided to corporate customers’ employees under long-term rental arrangements.
The financing represents an important shift in Everphone’s capital structure.
For the first time, the company is using a corporate loan based on its overall creditworthiness rather than financing secured against individual pools of devices.
The transaction builds on Everphone’s roughly 10-year relationship with Commerzbank, which serves as its primary bank.
KfW is participating through its Venture Tech Growth Financing program.
The participation marks KfW’s second financing involving Everphone following an earlier transaction in 2023 and 2024.
Everphone said the new financing structure significantly reduces its refinancing costs.
The interest margin is approximately 20 basis points lower than under its previous financing.
Because financing costs represent a major component of unit economics in Device-as-a-Service, the company said the reduced margin directly improves profitability.
Longer financing terms are also expected to allow Everphone to purchase larger device volumes at lower unit costs.
This is particularly important for replacement devices, which Everphone provides to customers at no additional charge when hardware fails.
The lower financing costs contributed to Everphone reporting positive earnings before taxes for the first time in August 2026.
KEY QUOTES:
“Everphone demonstrates how technology, the circular economy, and a scalable business model can be combined. We are delighted to contribute with our purchasing financing to enabling Everphone to capitalize on its growth opportunities and expand its market position further.”
Mirjam Kuppe-Klötzer, Senior Specialist Corporate Lending at Commerzbank Corporate Clients
“Especially during the growth phase, scale-ups need financing solutions that combine speed and predictability. This is precisely where we come in with KfW’s Venture Tech Growth Financing together with Commerzbank, supporting Everphone in positioning itself as an integral tech and sustainability partner for its customers.”
Jochen Eichmann, Head of Venture Tech Growth Financing at KfW
“Profitability in Device-as-a-Service is achieved at the unit economics level, and financing costs are one of the biggest items there. Our corporate finance team has set up several facilities in recent years, reducing the interest margin with every round. The structure with Commerzbank and KfW represents the biggest step yet for inventory.”
Veronika von Heise-Rotenburg, CFO of Everphone
